item.title: Nigeria’s net reserves hit $34.8bn in 2025 - Cardoso
item.description: Olayemi Cardoso, governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), says Nigeria’s net foreign exchange reserves (NEFR) at the end of 2025 were $34.80 billion — exceeding the country’s total gross reserves recorded in 2023. According to a statement on Monday, Cardoso disclosed the figure over the weekend. item.title: VIDEO: Asake surprises his mum with a luxury G-Wagon
item.description: Asake, the Grammy-nominated Nigerian music star, has surprised his mother with a brand-new G-Wagon G63. In a now-viral video, the ‘Mr Money’ hitmaker is seen overflowing with joy as he embraces his mother before presenting her with the keys to the luxury SUV. Overcome with emotion, his mother beams with delight as she takes in the stunning white vehicle. item.title: Diddy set for earlier prison release
item.description: Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs, the US rapper, is reportedly set to be released from prison about six weeks earlier than previously scheduled as he continues his appeal against a four-year sentence. According to public records of the Federal Bureau of Prisons cited by Page Six, Combs’ projected release date has been adjusted from June 4, 2028, to April 25, 2028. item.title: Medical council suspends Euracare’s director, two doctors over death of Chimamanda’s son
item.description: The Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN) investigation panel has suspended Euracare’s medical director and two doctors over the death of Chimamanda Adichie’s son. Nkanu Adichie-Esege, one of Adichie’s twins, died on January 7, 2026, following complications during a series of preparatory medical procedures. item.title: Passengers escape death as BRT bus catches fire in Lagos
item.description: file photo Passengers aboard a Bus Rapid Transit, BRT, vehicle escaped death on Tuesday after the bus was engulfed by fire while in motion on the Mile 12 Bridge along Ikorodu Road in Lagos. Eyewitness accounts indicated that the incident occurred mid-morning, with the high-capacity bus suddenly bursting into flames during the journey. item.title: Sit-at-home: Anambra Govt slashes workers salaries for failing to work on Mondays
item.description: Anambra State Government has made good its threat to slash salaries of workers who failed to show up for work on Mondays due to the sit-at-home ordered by separatist elements in the South-East.
